conv.u: explain the difference between ser and estar
conv.reply: Ser vs. estar (Ser y estar)Spanish splits English 'to be' into two verbs.1. Ser: identity, profession and category — Use ser to say who or what someone or something is: name, job, nationality, religion, relationship, or any noun that classifies.e.g. Mi vecina es enfermera en el Hospital Santo Tomás. — My neighbour is a nurse at Santo Tomás Hospital.2. Ser: defining characteristics — Use ser for qualities that describe what someone or something is like: personality, appearance, size, colour, inherent nature.e.g. El Canal es enorme y muy antiguo. — The Canal is enormous and very old.3. Ser: origin, material and possession — Ser + de expresses where someone comes from, the material of an object, and its owner.e.g. Rubén Blades es de la ciudad de Panamá. — Rubén Blades is from Panama City.4. Time, dates and amounts — Ser gives the hour, the day, the date and totals; estar a/en positions you in time.e.g. Es la una y media; ya es hora de almorzar. — It's half past one; it's time for lunch.5. Ser: where and when events happen — An event (party, meeting, concert, wedding, exam) 'takes place', so its location and time use ser.e.g. El concierto es en el Teatro Nacional. — The concert is (takes place) at the National Theatre.6. Estar: location and position — Use estar for where people and objects are, even if the location never changes, and for body position.e.g. El Biomuseo está en Amador. — The Biomuseo is in Amador.…5 more in the full guide (Grammar guides › Ser vs. estar).Say quiz me and I’ll quiz you on it, one question at a time.
